description: Three neuron circuits with each output normalled round into the next one's input, making a feedback ring that runs with nothing patched

params.text: Adds a steady 0V to 5V into that neuron's mix before the mix is rectified
Sets the size of that neuron's comparator swing, 1V to 10V; that much is taken off the rectified mix while the mix is above 0V and added to it while it is not
Scales whatever reaches the IN jack below it, passing nothing fully anticlockwise and full level fully clockwise; with that jack empty it scales the neighbouring neuron's output instead

inputs.text: Feeds neuron 1 through the IN knob above it; with nothing patched that knob passes neuron 3's output instead
Added into neuron 1 and neuron 2 at once, at full level and with no knob in the way
Feeds neuron 2 through the IN knob above it; with nothing patched that knob passes neuron 1's output instead
Added into neuron 2 and neuron 3 at once, at full level and with no knob in the way, despite the jack's tooltip naming neurons 3 and 4
Feeds neuron 3 through the IN knob above it; with nothing patched that knob passes neuron 2's output instead
Added straight into neuron 1's mix at full level, with no knob in the way
Added straight into neuron 2's mix at full level, with no knob in the way
Added straight into neuron 3's mix at full level, with no knob in the way

outputs.text: That neuron's mix, clamped to 0V to 10V, with its comparator swing applied
Neuron 1 plus neuron 3 less neuron 2 while that difference is negative, down to -10V, and 0V at any other time
Neuron 1 plus neuron 3 less neuron 2 while that difference is positive, up to 10V, and 0V at any other time

notes: the three IN knobs come up fully anticlockwise, which breaks the feedback ring; until one is raised each neuron output rests at whatever its REACT knob is set to.
raising the IN knobs is all it takes to make sound: the ring has no clock and needs nothing patched, and the loop is one sample long, so changing Rack's sample rate changes what comes out.
a cable in an IN jack replaces the neighbouring neuron's output at that point rather than adding to it, which opens the ring at that neuron.
